scope: Metrics regex postings unions and tenant-wide exact posting identities. Index microbenchmarks, not native service performance qualification.

environment.shared_host: Existing demo broker, schema registry and three demo apps continue running. No compilers or profilers run during paired timing. Environment refreshes interrupted builds and one incomplete timing pass; incomplete results are excluded.
environment.round_note: Workspace reconnected after initial correctness checks and allocation captures completed; no executing build, profile or timing was interrupted. CPU quota, affinity and kernel unchanged. Initial allocation captures overlapped native Pyroscope checks; final recaptures overlapped a Cargo rebuild. CPU captures and final paired timings wait for compilers, other profilers and native test containers to finish. Existing demo containers remain running.

algorithm.baseline: Repeated BTreeSet insertion for matching value postings; sequential broad exact posting cloning followed by regex intersection.
algorithm.candidate: One bulk BTreeSet collection over matching postings and missing-label fingerprints. When the smallest non-empty exact posting covers every tenant series and there is one broad regex, start with the regex result. Other broad selectors and invalid matchers keep sequential fallback.
algorithm.upstream: Pinned Mimir posting unions use a streaming loser tree over sorted posting iterators. Krabka still materializes an owned tree; this change does not implement that iterator API.

profiles.query_count_note: Each metric allocation trace includes the verification query, so query count is iterations + 1. Three literal job equality counts verify the regex result outside resolve_query and are excluded from wrapper-filtered allocation counts.
profiles.cpu_scope: Whole process captures include fixture construction and drop; generic symbols can fold and DWARF recovery is incomplete. Whole-capture percentages are diagnostics, not exact query CPU costs.

baseline_query_samples.note: Only samples whose recovered stack contains resolve_query are counted. Incomplete stacks and merged generic symbols prevent exact CPU attribution.

refined_query_samples.note: Only samples whose recovered stack contains resolve_query are counted. Incomplete stacks and merged generic symbols prevent exact CPU attribution.

initial_candidate.reason: Additional regex-position checks in the common selective loop consistently slowed small selectors. First two clean pairs show 10–17% regressions in several controls; move the new planning to a separate function.
initial_candidate.timing_note: Three initial pairs were captured. Pair 3 overlapped the cached formatter for the refinement, so only pairs 1 and 2 support the initial regression decision. All raw results are preserved.

timing.baseline_note: Final first-round metric timing binary; same fixture, harness and compiler flags.

profiles.query_count_note: Each metric allocation trace includes the verification query, so query count is iterations + 1. Three literal job equality counts verify the regex result outside resolve_query and are excluded from wrapper-filtered allocation counts.
profiles.cpu_scope: Whole process captures include fixture construction and drop; generic symbols can fold and DWARF recovery is incomplete. Whole-capture percentages are diagnostics, not exact query CPU costs.

baseline_query_samples.note: Only samples whose recovered stack contains resolve_query are counted. Incomplete stacks and merged generic symbols prevent exact CPU attribution.

refinement.implementation: Restore the original any-regex guard and ordinary selective loop; handle tenant-wide broad regexes in a separate non-inlined function.
refinement.pilot: Two alternating pairs over six IDs; selective controls have roughly 2–7% positive ratios, negative-regex control mixed, broad regex reduced to 6–8 ms. These preliminary numbers do not replace the final full sweep.

verification.scope_note: Final isolated regex path. Unit optimization level 1 with cached Cargo dependency fingerprints; Cargo release public integrations rebuilt against the final root library.

paired_timing.baseline_note: Final first-round metric timing binary; same fixture, harness and compiler flags.

decision.basis: Large broad-regex timing and query allocation reductions repeat. Accept the recorded 12-18% smaller absent-label regressions, about 8-19 ns in median run means, as a tradeoff. Other controls are mixed. This does not qualify native-service CPU, memory or latency.

limitations: Shared four-CPU host with existing demo workload; same CPU pin and alternating timing order.
Criterion has ten samples per case and three independent pairs; confidence intervals and raw samples are preserved.
Instrumented CPU elapsed time is separate from unprofiled timings; sampled wrapper periods are incomplete-stack lower bounds.
Allocation traces overlap the documented native test or build jobs; counts are wrapper-filtered and establish no process RSS reduction.
No final-source large native-service speed comparison against Mimir, Loki, Tempo or Pyroscope. Native oracle checks cover semantics only.
Existing 85 numeric benchmark budgets are unchanged; the 76 new IDs remain unseeded pending the recorded stable runner.

evidence_manifest.scope: All raw evidence files below 100 MB; complete profiling driver hashes and the initial driver archive are recorded separately.
